results.title: The Cloud GPU Price War 2026: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers
highlights:
Is there a cloud GPU price war in 2026? Yes — but not the one the headlines imply. The real 2026 story is a split market: specialist “neocloud” providers (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Together AI, RunPod) list on-demand GPUs far below the hyperscalers — a rented H100 starts around $2.89/GPU-hour on a neocloud versus roughly $7–$12/GPU-hour on AWS, Azure, or GCP. Yet reserved, contract, and new Blackwell-generation prices actually rose through the first half of 2026. The war is about who wins list-price comparisons, not about a broad price collapse.

...

TL;DR — The 2026 GPU price war in one glance

- Neoclouds list an on-demand H100 from ~$2.89/hr (RunPod) to ~$3.99/hr (Together AI); Nebius lists $3.85/GPU-hr
- Hyperscaler list prices are far higher: AWS p5 works out to ~$6.88/GPU-hr, Azure ND H100 v5 to ~$12.29/GPU-hr (third-party trackers; not confirmed on primary pages)
- One Aug 2026 report puts neocloud rentals up to 66% below the large incumbent clouds
- But contract prices rose: SemiAnalysis' H100 1-year index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hr (Mar 2026)
- CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% across SKUs in July 2026 and called capacity “effectively sold out”
- AWS quietly raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% on Jan 4, 2026 — reportedly its first EC2 GPU price increase in ~two decades
- Nebius disclosed a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price
- Net: spot/older-Hopper pricing softened; premium, reserved, and Blackwell pricing firmed or rose

...

Here is the part that breaks the “prices are crashing” narrative. The single best independent data series on GPU rental pricing — SemiAnalysis' H100 rental index, built from a continuously-collected, composition-resistant weighted mean across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and GPU marketplaces — shows the opposite of a collapse for contract capacity. Its 1-year contract H100 range climbed from roughly $1.70/GPU-hour in October 2025 toward $2.35/GPU-hour by March 2026, with the spot-contract composite index sitting around $2.82/GPU-hour in April 2026 and on-demand capacity marked “sold out” since February (SemiAnalysis H100 index, 2026).

The top of SemiAnalysis' 1-year contract range rose through H1 2026 as premium capacity sold out — the clearest counter-evidence to a broad price war.

...

## The 2026 price hikes nobody announced

If 2026 were a price war, you would expect a run of press-released cuts. Instead, the documented pricing events of 2026 are mostly increases — several delivered quietly.

CoreWeave — ~25% list-price increase across SKUs (July 2026)

On its Q2 2026 earnings call (August 11, 2026), CoreWeave disclosed “an approximately 25% increase across SKUs in response to the current demand environment,” adding that pricing and margins for Blackwell and Vera Rubin SKUs were “setting new highs” while prior-generation SKUs sat at or above prior levels. Management described near-term capacity as “effectively sold out” (CoreWeave Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Revenue hit $2.58B, up 112% year over year, on a $104B backlog.

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/hr — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). Treat the exact figures as multiply-reported rather than primary-confirmed.

Nebius — record Blackwell auction clearing price (Q2 2026)

Nebius reported group revenue up more than 450% year over year and a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price, alongside a swing to positive adjusted EBITDA (Nebius Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Not the behavior of a provider slashing prices to win share.

results.title: Nvidia H100 GPU rental costs surge 50% in six months as AI demand outpaces supply
results.author: Editorial Team
highlights:
Renting Nvidia’s workhorse AI chip just got a lot more expensive. The cost of H100 GPU rentals climbed roughly 40% between October 2025 and March 2026, according to data from SemiAnalysis, with average rates jumping from $1.70 per GPU-hour to $2.35 per GPU-hour. And if you want to actually get your hands on a cluster of these chips, you’re looking at 12 to 18 months of waiting.

The price spike represents a sharp reversal from the trend that defined much of 2025, when GPU rental prices dropped more than 60% from their 2023-2024 peaks.

...

Inference workloads and multi-agent AI systems have pushed compute requirements well beyond what the existing supply base can handle. On-demand H100 capacity is effectively sold out across Neoclouds and hyperscalers alike.

Even modest deployments have become hard to secure. Clusters as small as 8 nodes, or 64 GPUs, are increasingly difficult to procure on short notice.

February 2026 saw particularly aggressive price moves, with 15-20% increases recorded in a single month as providers adjusted to the new demand reality.

The broader market for on-demand H100 rentals now spans a wide range, from $2.19 to over $4 per GPU-hour depending on the provider and whether the capacity is reserved in advance or purchased on the spot.

...

For GPU cloud providers, higher utilization rates and rising prices translate to improved revenue per rack. Companies that locked in long-term supply agreements with Nvidia at favorable terms are sitting on what amounts to a spread trade: cheap wholesale, expensive retail.

Hyperscalers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure have the balance sheets to absorb temporary margin compression, but smaller Neoclouds may find themselves in a stronger negotiating position than expected. When every GPU is spoken for, the provider with available capacity has leverage regardless of brand name.

results.title: Old hardware is supposed to get cheaper with time. GPUs are breaking that rule. | Piyush Somani
results.author: Piyush Somani
highlights:
Old hardware is supposed to get cheaper with time. GPUs are breaking that rule.

The rental price of an Nvidia H100 has climbed to $2.71/hour, up from $1.96 just last November — a nearly 40% jump in under a year, with forward pricing curving even higher into 2027 and 2028.

Baseten recently shared that its cloud provider is raising B200 rental pricing from $2.63/hour to $5.10/hour when the contract renews in October. Nearly double.

And CoreWeave just locked in a contract for Nvidia's A100 - a chip launched in 2020 - running all the way out to 2029, calling the pricing "attractive."

In every other category of infrastructure, the oldest generation is the cheapest one on the shelf. Right now, in GPU capacity, it's the opposite.

results.title: H100 GPU Rental Prices Ended October at $3.00+ | Lines.com | Lines.com
results.author: Dr. Sarah Okonkwo
highlights:
Updated November 2, 2026 6 min read 

 Resolution Verdict 

 YES Market Resolved 

Market has ended. Final implied probability: 100%.

...

H100 GPU rental prices settled at exactly $3.00 per GPU-hour on October 31, 2026, according to the Ornn Compute Price Index, triggering resolution of the $3.00+ outcome in this Polymarket market. The benchmark, which tracks transacted rental prices across the neocloud market, confirmed the figure at the daily 12:00 AM ET settle. The historical base rate suggests commodity compute benchmarks rarely land precisely at a threshold boundary, making this a statistically notable resolution.

...

## H100 Rental Prices Confirmed Above $3.00 at October Close

The Ornn Compute Price Index (OCPI-H100) settled at $3.00 per GPU-hour on October 31, 2026, the final day of the resolution window. The index tracks exclusively transacted rental prices across neocloud providers, not list prices or estimates, making it a transaction-based benchmark. The $3.00 figure satisfied the market’s top outcome bracket, which required end-of-October pricing to reach or exceed that level. Earlier in October, the OCPI-H100 had settled at $2.79 per GPU-hour on October 2, meaning prices climbed roughly 7.5% across the month before hitting the threshold.

The broader provider landscape corroborated the index reading. Runpod listed H100 SXM at $3.99 per hour. Lambda’s 8-GPU H100 SXM instance listed at $3.99 per GPU-hour, up from $2.99 in a prior snapshot. Market-median pricing across all providers ranged from $3.25 to $3.28 per hour in September, establishing an upward trajectory into October. The data tells a clear story: neocloud supply remained tight enough relative to AI compute demand to sustain prices above the $3.00 benchmark through month-end.

The final probability at close reached 100.0%, converging from an opening-day price of 35 cents. A 10.7% single-day move on October 31 reflected the market absorbing the imminent settlement confirmation. The trajectory was not a gradual drift but a decisive repricing as the resolution window closed.

...

The $3.00+ outcome opened at 35 cents implied probability, meaning traders initially assessed roughly a one-in-three chance that H100 spot prices would reach the top bracket by October’s end. That opening price was a significant underestimate. The Ornn OCPI-H100 had already settled at $2.92 per GPU-hour on October 1, just $0.08 below the resolution threshold, and the broader market median sat at $3.25 to $3.28 per hour in September. Within the confidence interval of available data, the market underpriced the $3.00+ outcome at inception by a measurable margin.

...

The $3.00 per GPU-hour settlement on the Ornn OCPI-H100 carries structural significance beyond a single market resolution. GPU rental rates at or above $3.00 per hour represent a persistent premium over the spot-floor prices available on marketplace platforms like Vast.ai, where rates begin near $1.49 per hour. That spread between spot floor and index benchmark reflects the persistent demand for guaranteed, enterprise-grade H100 access from AI model developers and infrastructure operators. Mordor Intelligence sized the GPU rental market at roughly $52 billion in 2026, up from $34.6 billion in 2025, providing the demand context that sustained prices through October.

...

- Ornn OCPI-H100 settled at exactly $3.00 on October 31, sitting precisely at the lower bound of the resolved bracket. Any further softening in neocloud supply or demand moderation could push the index below $3.00 in subsequent months.
- Lambda’s H100 SXM list price moved from $2.99 to $3.99 per GPU-hour, a 33% increase, suggesting provider pricing power remains intact heading into the fourth quarter of 2026.
- The GPU rental market’s projected growth toward $199 billion by 2031 implies that structural demand pressure on H100 and successor chips will persist, supporting elevated rental benchmarks beyond the October 2026 window.
- CME Group’s listing of Silicon Data H100 futures on October 5, 2026 introduces a regulated price discovery mechanism that could reduce the kind of inception-pricing inefficiency this Polymarket market exhibited.

results.title: OvhCloud augmente ses prix pour la deuxième fois en 2026 - ZDNET
results.author: Louis Adam
highlights:
OvhCloud a publié hier le détail de ses nouveaux tarifs au second semestre 2026. Comme l'avait annoncé Octave Klaba, la hausse des prix des composants et de la RAM se répercute sur les fournisseurs de services cloud.

...

Publié le 18/08/2026 à 12:30 | Mis à jour le 02/09/2026 à 14:31 

 

Ce n'est pas une surprise, mais ça n'est jamais agréable : OvhCloud a publié hier le détail des évolutions de sa grille tarifaire pour le second semestre 2026, et la facture se révèle salée. Les hausses affectent les offres Baremetal et Public Cloud, mais la société précise que ses offres d'entrée de gamme, Kimsufi, So You Start et Rise ne sont pas affectées.

## Des augmentations à partir de septembre

En moyenne, les prix augmentent de 28% pour les offres s'appuyant sur des équipements de la Gen 2024, et de 51% sur la Gen 2026. Les nouveaux prix s'appliqueront aux configurations de serveur à partir du 1er septembre. Mais les augmentations affecteront également le matériel déjà en production à compter du 1er octobre, sur les gammes Advance, Game, Scale et High Grade.

Octave Klaba avait annoncé l'augmentation des prix à venir dans un message sur X en début de semaine dernière. Le fondateur de la société expliquait alors que la hausse de ces tarifs était poussée par l'augmentation des prix de la RAM et des équipements que la société utilise pour fournir ses clients. Il déplore une situation très frustrante, mais rappelle qu'OVHCloud fait son possible pour limiter la hausse des prix et rester transparent à l'égard de ses clients.

...

L'enjeu pour OVHCloud est de taille : "le contexte mondial nous impose une discipline très stricte pour, tout simplement, continuer à livrer les nouvelles commandes" résume Octave Klaba. Et la situation ne devrait pas s'améliorer tout de suite : le dirigeant estime que l'augmentation devrait continuer en 2027, voire plus tard. "Nous pensons que cette situation va durer jusqu'en 2028, avec un retour à la normale espéré en 2029" veut croire Octave Klaba. Pour limiter l'impact de futures augmentations, le dirigeant invite ses clients à souscrire à des offres longues durées, payées à l'avance, avant le 1er octobre.

Au début de l'année 2026, OvhCloud avait déjà annoncé une première série d'augmentation de ses tarifs afin de s'adapter aux évolutions du prix des composants qui augmentent régulièrement depuis plusieurs mois. Cette première hausse des prix, dévoilée au mois de février, affectait là aussi les mêmes offres en épargnant l'entrée de gamme. D'autres acteurs concurrents d'OvhCloud comme le groupe allemand Hetzner, avait lui aussi annoncé début avril une augmentation de ses tarifs liée à la pression sur les prix de la mémoire RAM

## Avantage aux gros poissons

Cette augmentation est principalement liée à l'essor des technologies d'intelligence artificielle, très consommatrice en matière de mémoire RAM et de puissance de calcul, et dont les principaux acteurs accaparent une part grandissante de la production mondiale.

Cette situation affecte mécaniquement tous les fournisseurs de cloud, mais les plus gros acteurs peuvent plus facilement se permettre de jouer la montre.

Du côté d'AWS, la société a annoncé une hausse mesurée du prix de ses GPU en début d'année 2026, et Microsoft revoyait à la hausse les tarifs de ses offres Office 365 au début du mois de juillet, mais pas de hausse généralisée pour l'instant. Les analystes s'attendent néanmoins à ce que les tensions sur les prix des composants finissent par se répercuter sur l'ensemble des acteurs.

results.title: Truist Raises CoreWeave Price Target to $165 on Strategic Pricing Response | Gate News
results.author: GateMacroTradfiHub
highlights:
Key Takeaways

- Truist Securities raised CoreWeave price target to $165 on August 24 citing strategic pricing response.
- CoreWeave raised rental prices 25% in July to offset NVIDIA's 15%+ GPU price increases.
- CoreWeave's contribution margin projected to expand from 24% to 33% in H2 this year.

Truist Securities maintained its 'Buy' rating on CoreWeave (NAS:CRWV) and raised the price target from $155 to $165, according to CNBC on August 24 (local time). Analyst Arvind Ramnani attributed the upgrade to CoreWeave's strategic pricing response: the company raised rental prices for all products by 25% in July, fully offsetting NVIDIA's (NAS:NVDA) 15%+ price increase on its latest GPUs driven by surging AI-driven demand for memory and storage devices. The AI computing infrastructure supply shortage continues to support premium pricing across the sector, with CoreWeave's price adjustments taking effect in H2 this year while NVIDIA's increases apply to systems shipping early next year, including Blackwell and Vera Rubin lineups.

...

Arvind Ramnani of Truist Securities analyzed that NVIDIA raised prices on its latest GPUs by more than 15% due to the AI boom driving surging demand for memory and storage devices, while CoreWeave raised rental prices for all products by 25% in July to fully offset this increase. The analyst noted that NVIDIA's price increases concentrate on systems shipping early next year, including the Blackwell and Vera Rubin latest lineups, whereas CoreWeave's price increase effects will be immediately reflected in results starting H2 this year.

results.title: Ornn Wants Wall Street to Trade AI Compute Prices Like Oil - Startup Fortune
results.author: Janet Harrison
highlights:
Ornn is the startup trying to supply that number. Founded in 2025 by Kush Bavaria and Wayne Nelms, who a16z crypto says met at MIT, the New York company publishes the Ornn Compute Price Index, a transaction-based benchmark for GPU rental prices. Its own April announcement said the index had been added to the Bloomberg Terminal and was already being used by more than 400 data center operators, investors and AI companies.

The Blackwell price spike is the hook. Several outlets citing Ornn's index reported that renting an advanced Nvidia Blackwell GPU rose to $4.08 an hour in April, up 48% from $2.75 two months earlier. That isn't gentle movement for infrastructure sold as on-demand capacity. If you're an AI company running agents that call tools, retry tasks and burn through tokens all day, that price is not an abstraction. It lands in your monthly bill.

...

Intercontinental Exchange announced on May 19 that it planned to launch U.S. dollar, cash-settled GPU compute futures tied to Ornn's Compute Price Index, pending regulatory approval. The contracts are meant to settle against live-traded spot prices for GPU compute across major hardware types, not a cloud provider's posted rate card.

CME Group has now moved too. On August 11, it said it would launch Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures and Silicon Data B200 Rental Index Futures on October 5, 2026, also pending regulatory review. Each contract will represent a month's worth of rent for the relevant Nvidia GPU, using hourly rental-rate indexes published by Silicon Data.

results.title: B200 GPU Rental Prices Hit $7.50+ by End of September | Lines.com | Lines.com
results.author: Dr. Sarah Okonkwo
highlights:
NVIDIA B200 GPU rental prices cleared the $7.50-per-hour threshold by the end of September 2026, resolving the market’s top outcome bracket as confirmed. The OCPI-B200 index, a benchmark built from transacted neocloud deals, settled at $7.71 per GPU-hour on October 4, 2026, confirming that the $7.50+ band held through the resolution window ending October 1, 2026. The data tells a clear story: B200 compute costs rose sharply through Q3 2026 after entering September at $5.62.

...

The Silicon Data SDB200RT index entered September 2026 at $5.62 per GPU-hour, up 27.6% year to date through August. From that starting point, B200 spot rates accelerated through the final weeks of the month. The OCPI-B200 benchmark, sourced from transacted neocloud deals rather than scraped rate cards, confirmed a settlement of $7.71 per GPU-hour in early October. That figure placed the end-of-September reading firmly within the $7.50+ resolution bracket, triggering a YES outcome across the top tier of this multi-outcome market.

...

B200 rental prices clearing $7.50 per hour marks a significant inflection for enterprise AI infrastructure budgets. The neocloud sector, led by providers such as CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, and emerging platforms, is now pricing Blackwell-generation compute well above initial market expectations from early 2026. Procurement teams modeling AI training and inference costs for 2027 must revise upward. The gap between on-demand and spot pricing, with spot running as low as $1.77 per hour on some platforms even as on-demand cleared $7.50, creates meaningful optionality for workload-flexible buyers.

...

- NVIDIA Blackwell GPU supply constraints through Q4 2026 are likely to sustain elevated B200 spot rates, given that hyperscaler reservation pipelines remain tight and neocloud providers face similar allocation pressures.
- The spread between on-demand B200 rates (above $7.50) and spot rates (below $2.00 on some platforms) signals a two-tier market that prediction market designers should model as separate questions rather than a single price index.
- Enterprises anchoring 2027 AI compute budgets to pre-Q3 2026 B200 reference prices face material forecast error, with the index up more than 37% from its September 1 entry point to its October 4 confirmed settlement.
- Polymarket’s related markets, including IPO and acquisition timelines at 100% and Anthropic valuation markers at 100%, suggest traders in AI-adjacent markets are pricing a sustained infrastructure boom with high confidence through 2027.
